macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Canada retaliates after U.S. tariff escalation
items.summary: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion of U.S. goods after President Trump said tariffs on Canadian-made cars, trucks and auto parts would rise to 50% at the start of 2027. The move intensified trade-war fears and was cited as a market-moving headwind for bonds and equities.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as oil prices fall and bond-market stress eases
items.summary: Wall Street posted modest gains, with the S&P 500 up 0.2%, the Dow up 107 points, and the Nasdaq 0.4% higher in afternoon trading. Reuters said falling oil prices helped ease bond-market worries and support stocks.

items.title: Treasury buyback news helps calm markets; yields slide
items.summary: Reuters reported that recent U.S. Treasury buyback announcements helped pull yields lower, with the 10-year yield posting its biggest fall in two months in Monday trading. Lower yields and steadier markets supported the broader risk mood.

items.title: Global markets wait for Nvidia earnings
items.summary: Reuters said investors were bracing for Nvidia’s results after the close, with the stock seen as a key driver for broader market sentiment. The report also noted Bitcoin crossed $80,000 for the first time since mid-May amid a strong recent rally.

items.title: U.S. consumer confidence weakens
items.summary: Chinese-language market coverage said U.S. consumer confidence fell to a seven-month low, with respondents more pessimistic about business conditions and employment prospects. That reinforced concerns about the underlying U.S. economic outlook.

items.title: German business confidence improves and GDP beats estimates
items.summary: Germany’s Ifo business climate index rose to 88.8 in August from a revised 86.7, and second-quarter GDP expanded 0.3% quarter over quarter, both above expectations. The data suggested the euro-area recovery is still intact.

items.title: Markets await U.S. data and Fed commentary
items.summary: Reuters said traders were watching U.S. consumer confidence, new-home sales, Richmond Fed surveys, and remarks from Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin. The same calendar also highlighted a U.S. Treasury auction and corporate earnings from Intuit.

items.title: Nvidia, Moderna, and Indian stocks in focus
items.summary: Market wrap coverage said U.S. stocks rose with Nvidia up more than 2%, while Moderna jumped 14% after multiple Wall Street target upgrades. Separate coverage also noted Indian benchmark indices closed higher, with the Sensex and Nifty both advancing.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly tops $81,000 as crypto rally extends
items.summary: Bitcoin surged to a three-month high above $81,000 before trimming gains, while Ether, XRP, Solana, Cardano, and BNB also advanced. The move was linked to dollar कमजोरी, Treasury buyback expectations, ETF inflows, and short covering.

items.title: Bitcoin pulls back after crossing $81,000 amid extreme greed sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin retreated to around $78,933 after touching $81.2K, and overall crypto market capitalization eased from a 24-hour peak of $2.71 trillion. The report also noted heavy short liquidations and the Crypto Fear and Greed Index staying at extreme greed.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows and Treasury moves help drive BTC above $80,000
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly traded above $80,000, with the rally attributed to renewed spot ETF inflows, improving risk appetite, and short covering in derivatives markets. The report said Treasury bond-buyback plans were part of the broader macro backdrop.

items.title: Crypto rally gains momentum as Bitcoin nears $81,000 and altcoins surge
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 4.6% on the day in one report, while Ether, XRP, Solana, Cardano, Dogecoin, and Shiba Inu also posted strong weekly gains. The piece framed the move as a broad risk-on rebound across digital assets.

items.title: Solana outpaces Bitcoin on strong ETF demand
items.summary: Solana traded around $98 and outperformed Bitcoin as crypto ETF inflows reached about $1.2 billion in a single day, according to the report. The article highlighted Solana’s relative strength versus Bitcoin in the latest session.

items.title: Crypto ETFs continued to attract capital, led by broad-based demand
items.summary: U.S.-listed crypto ETFs gathered roughly $192.6 million in new investments on August 24, with products tied to Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, and Hyperliquid. The report said Bitcoin inflows slowed while demand for Solana products increased.

items.title: XRP and Ripple-related news keep attention on tokenization use cases
items.summary: A market note said JPMorgan is reportedly using parts of its tokenization business on the XRP Ledger, reinforcing interest in real-world settlement and tokenization applications. The same report linked XRP’s rally to Treasury buyback policy rather than a direct crypto-specific announcement.

items.title: Large holders reportedly realize record Bitcoin profits after rebound
items.summary: CryptoQuant commentary said large holders realized record profits of about $1.2 billion after Bitcoin moved back above their average cost basis. This suggests profit-taking may be emerging after the latest price surge.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI slows development of its most advanced model and tightens controls
items.summary: OpenAI said it is reducing the pace of work on its most advanced AI model while overhauling research and training systems and adding stronger internal safeguards after a recent security incident involving one of its models. The move signals a broader shift toward tighter governance around frontier model development.

items.title: Apple launches faster Mac mini and Mac Studio to ride the AI boom
items.summary: Apple unveiled updated Mac mini and Mac Studio systems with new chips, positioning the computers for users running AI agents and heavier on-device workloads. The launch also underscores Apple’s push to make its hardware more attractive for AI development and deployment.

items.title: Google expands Gemini Enterprise for law firms and lawyers
items.summary: Google added new tools to its Gemini Enterprise platform aimed at lawyers and law firms, targeting legal-sector demand for AI assistants and workflow automation. The expansion reflects intensifying competition among major tech firms for enterprise AI customers.

items.title: Murf AI launches Falcon 2 text-to-speech model
items.summary: Murf AI introduced Falcon 2, a text-to-speech model designed for more human-like voices at lower cost and faster speed. The company says the system is aimed at enterprise use cases such as call centers, banks, and airlines.

items.title: Alibaba raises $10.2 billion to fund AI expansion
items.summary: Alibaba completed a HK$80 billion share placement to finance AI-related development, reinforcing its heavy spending in the sector. The fundraising comes amid intensifying competition in China’s AI market and broader U.S.-China tech rivalry.

items.title: TCS and Porsche sign AI deployment deal tied to major IT acquisition
items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services will acquire Porsche AG’s IT consulting subsidiary MHP as part of a broader partnership that includes a five-year agreement to deploy AI across Porsche’s engineering, manufacturing, operations, and customer-experience businesses. The deal highlights continued enterprise demand for applied AI.

items.title: Australia bans wholly AI-generated tracks from official music charts
items.summary: Australia’s recorded music industry said AI-generated songs will not be eligible for the ARIA Charts. The policy is one of the clearest recent industry responses to generative AI’s impact on creative markets.

items.title: Taiwan charges nine in illegal AI server export case
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people, including workers tied to Nvidia and Super Micro, over alleged illegal exports of high-end AI servers to China. The case highlights ongoing scrutiny of AI hardware supply chains and export controls.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Uber launches livestream ride safety feature for teens
items.summary: Uber rolled out an optional safety feature that lets parents or guardians watch a livestream of a teenager’s ride through the driver’s front-facing phone camera. The feature is aimed at giving families more visibility during teen trips.

items.title: Apple refreshes Mac mini and Mac Studio with new chips
items.summary: Apple introduced updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models featuring new M6 and M5 Ultra chips, adding a significant desktop hardware refresh to its product lineup. The launch is the biggest consumer-device announcement in the past day among the results provided.

items.title: SpaceX plans $100 billion rocket launch complex in Louisiana
items.summary: SpaceX said it will build a new Starship rocket launch complex in southern Louisiana, a major infrastructure expansion tied to future launch operations. The project was described as a roughly $100 billion effort.

items.title: TikTok parent ByteDance fined in Brazil over children’s data handling
items.summary: Brazil’s data protection regulator fined ByteDance more than 153 million reais, or nearly $30 million, over alleged failures in handling personal data for children and teenagers. The case adds to ongoing global scrutiny of platform privacy practices.

items.title: TikTok reaches $400 million settlement with U.S. Justice Department
items.summary: TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a U.S. Justice Department lawsuit tied to children’s privacy allegations. The deal closes a legal dispute stemming from claims involving its predecessor company, Musical.ly.

items.title: Dutch regulators hit Uber with nearly $1 billion fine
items.summary: Dutch data protection authorities fined Uber nearly $1 billion, saying the company used automated systems to suspend driver accounts without enough human review. The penalty is one of the largest recent regulatory actions against a major tech platform.

items.title: Tesla recalls nearly 3 million vehicles in China over door-handle safety risks
items.summary: Tesla is recalling about 2.98 million vehicles in China, including Model 3, Model Y, Model X, and Model S, over door-handle safety concerns. The recall is part of a broader wave of vehicle safety actions affecting the Chinese market.

items.title: Australia bans AI-generated tracks from official music charts
items.summary: Australia’s recorded music industry said songs wholly generated by AI will be excluded from official charts. The move reflects a growing policy response to AI-produced content in entertainment markets.

items.title: Taiwan charges 9 people over illegal AI server exports to China
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people, including one employee from Nvidia and two from Super Micro, over alleged illegal exports of high-end AI servers to China. The case underscores tightening export-control enforcement around advanced computing hardware.
